findings.claim: The 20 s request timeout does not cover reading the response body. `clearTimeout(timer)` runs in the `finally` attached to the fetch call (raydium_api.ts:139), i.e. as soon as the response HEADERS arrive, while `const text = await res.text()` runs afterwards unguarded. A stalled or drip-fed body (the real list-v2 pages are ~2.8 MB, docs/sources/discovery_apis.md §4) hangs the run with no timeout, no retry, no error and no log line, and it holds the serialized request queue behind it.
findings.evidence: /home/rares/trading/sol/atomarb/.scratch/review_discovery/02_timeout_body_hang.ts with timeoutMs=300, maxRetries=1 and a Response whose ReadableStream is never closed: `timeoutMs=300, maxRetries=1 -> after 3003 ms: STILL_HANGING`, `usage: 1 request(s) started, 0 error(s), 0 retries`. (With Node's real fetch, undici's own body timeout eventually applies, so in production this stretches the 20 s guarantee to undici's default rather than hanging forever, and a server sending one chunk per interval evades it entirely.)
findings.suggested_fix: Move `clearTimeout(timer)` after the body has been read — wrap both the fetch and `res.text()` in the same try/finally — so the AbortController covers header + body.

findings.claim: token2022Gate picks the Token-2022 transfer fee with the larger BASIS POINTS (line 148: `newer.bps > older.bps || (newer.bps === older.bps && newer.maxFee >= older.maxFee)`) and calls it "conservative" (line 145 comment and the `basis: max of older.../newer...` string). The fee is min(ceil(amount*bps/10000), maximum_fee), so when a scheduled fee update LOWERS bps and RAISES maximum_fee, the larger-bps entry is the SMALLER fee at real trade sizes. The adapter then under-charges the transfer fee and OVERSTATES Quote.amountOutToUser on a buy (and overstates the curve input, hence the WSOL out, on a sell). validatePool only warns (TOKEN2022_TRANSFER_FEE), so such a pool is quoted and traded.
